name: Brigand
body:
Brigandage is the life and practice of thieving and plunder, particularly in remote areas like mountains and forests. The only time you might see a band of brigands working together is during a particularly complicated score. On the other hand, for the right coin, or a cause they believe suits their lifestyle, a brigand will cooperate long enough to earn their place in an adventuring party.

Role: The brigand acts as a smart, suave raconteur when around potential marks. When confronted with potential opposition, he’s quick to become a threatening foe who can back up his boasts with his mastery of a favored weapon.

Alignment: Any non-lawful.

Hit Die: d8.

Parent Classes: Fighter and rogue.

Class Skills: The brigand’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Table: Brigand

Class Features

The following are class features of the brigand.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Brigands are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, as well as their favored weapon (see below). They are proficient with light armor, and with shields (except tower shields).

Brigand’s Cunning (Ex)

At 1st level, choose Dexterity, Wisdom, or Charisma. The brigand adds his Intelligence bonus to skill checks in place of the chosen ability modifier.

Favored Weapon (Ex)

The mark of a good brigand is in how well he is remembered by friend and foe alike; and there’s no easier way to earn quick recognition than through mastery of a signature weapon. Each brigand begins play with a masterwork weapon of his choice. If the weapon is exotic, he gains Exotic Weapon Proficiency as a bonus feat. Otherwise, he gains Weapon Focus with his favored weapon.

Size Up (Ex)

Brigands are thieves, yes; but they’re smart about who they fight. As a move action, a brigand can choose one creature he can see that has acted at least once in combat. When he hits that creature with his favored weapon, the brigand’s sneak attack damage becomes 1d6. At 3rd, 9th, and 16th level, the brigand increases his sneak attack damage by +1d6 when he hits a creature he has sized up. He can size up only one creature at a time.

At 9th level, the brigand can size a creature up as he moves toward it, even if it hasn’t yet acted in combat. At 16th level, when he sizes a creature up, it’s also flat-footed to the first attack he makes against it with his favored weapon.

Sneak Attack (Ex)

If a brigand can catch an opponent when it is unable to defend itself effectively from his attack, he can strike a vital spot for extra damage.

The brigand’s attack deals extra damage anytime his target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when the brigand flanks his target. This extra damage is 1d4 at 1st level, and increases to 1d6 at 2nd level. It increases by +1d6 at 5th level, and every 3 levels thereafter, as indicated on Table: Brigand. Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet. This additional damage is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit.

With a weapon that deals nonlethal damage (such as a sap, unarmed strike, or whip), a brigand can make a sneak attack that deals nonlethal damage instead of lethal damage. He cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a sneak attack—not even with the usual –4 penalty.

The brigand must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. A brigand cannot sneak attack while striking a creature with total concealment.

Keep Your Cool (Ex)

Brigands rarely lose their heads in combat; preferring instead to take those of their enemies. At 2nd level, a brigand gains Combat Expertise as a bonus feat. When he uses Combat Expertise with his favored weapon, the penalty he takes on attack rolls is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of +0). At 12th level, the penalty is reduced by 2, and at 20th level, the penalty is reduced by 3.

Alternatively, the brigand can take the feat’s normal penalty on to attacks and increase the dodge bonus it grants to his AC by +1, +2, and +3 in those same intervals.

Bonus Feats

At 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter, a brigand gains a bonus combat feat. The brigand treats his brigand levels as fighter levels when meeting the prerequisites of feats.

Danger Sense (Ex)

At 3rd level, a brigand gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against attacks made by traps.

In addition, he gains a +1 bonus on Perception checks to avoid being surprised by a foe. These bonuses increase by 1 every 3 brigand levels thereafter (to a maximum of +6 at 18th level).

This ability counts as trap sense for the purpose of any feat or class prerequisite, and can be replaced by any archetype class feature that replaces trap sense. The bonuses gained from this ability stack with those gained from trap sense (from another class).

Subtle Threat (Ex)

At 3rd level, the brigand is recognized well enough that he can make a subtle threat that puts a potential enemy off its game.

To use this ability, the brigand can’t be disguised or otherwise unrecognizable, and the creature he threatens must be within reach of his favored weapon and able to see or hear him.

Once the brigand makes a subtle threat, he can’t use it again on creatures that were present for the threat for 1 hour. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. The brigand can affect mindless creatures such as constructs, undead, and vermin, but they gain a +4 bonus on their saving throw.

When the brigand makes his subtle threat, he uses a free action to either give his target a dangerous look, or speak a few choice words that makes it doubt its safety. The target must succeed at a Will save against DC 10 + the brigand’s Bluff, Diplomacy, or Intimidate bonus. If the target is an animal or magical beast, the brigand can use his Handle Animal bonus instead.

If the target fails its save, it becomes demoralized any time the brigand isn’t within its clear line of sight. For this purpose, creatures between the target and the brigand break its clear line of sight. This lasts for 1 minute per brigand level.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 4th level, a brigand can react to danger before his senses would normally allow him to do so. He cannot be caught flat-footed, nor does he lose his Dexterity bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. He still loses his Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized.

A brigand with this ability can still lose his Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against him.

If a brigand already has uncanny dodge from a different class, he automatically gains improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Threatening Appearance (Ex)

At 5th level, a brigand learns to use an enemy’s fear to his advantage. The first time a brigand with this ability attempts an attack against a foe that saw or heard his subtle threat, the foe is treated as flat-footed for the rest of the brigand’s turn (uncanny dodge or a similar ability prevents this effect unless the brigand is at least 4 levels higher than the foe with uncanny dodge). If the foe was not the target of his subtle threat, it must be completely unaware of his presence (usually due to Stealth or invisibility).

The foe also takes a –4 penalty on attacks made against the brigand until the start of the brigand’s next turn.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 8th level, a brigand can no longer be flanked.

This defense denies another brigand the ability to sneak attack the character by flanking his, unless the attacker has at least four more brigand levels than the target does.

If a character already has uncanny dodge from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum brigand level required to flank the character.

Evasion (Ex)

At 10th level, a brigand can avoid even magical and unusual attacks with great agility. If he succeeds at a Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, he instead takes no damage. Evasion can be used only if the brigand is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless brigand does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Blatant Threat (Ex)

At 11th level, the brigand can affect a number of creatures up to his Intelligence modifier with his subtle threat. whenever the brigand makes an attack against a foe that failed its save against his subtle threat, that foe is becomes frightened for 1 round, in addition to being shaken as normal, unless the foe succeeds at a separate Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the brigand’s class level + his Charisma modifier).

Once a creature has been the target of this ability (either as the target of the attack or as a nearby creature, regardless of whether or not it was successful), it is immune to that brigand’s blatant threats for 24 hours. This effect is in addition to the bonuses gained from the threatening appearance ability. This is a mind-affecting fear effect.

Great Allure (Ex)

At 13th level, the danger of being around a brigand is as intoxicating as being wooed by one. The brigand gains a bonus equal to 1/2 his brigand level on all Charisma-based skill checks.

This bonus doesn’t apply to his subtle threats.

Stunning Appearance (Ex)

At 17th level, a brigand can leave his foes unable to respond when he appears. Whenever a brigand with this ability makes a successful attack against a foe that is unaware of the brigand’s presence (see threatening appearance), the foe must make a successful Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the brigand’s class level + his Charisma modifier) or be stunned until the end of the brigand’s next turn. If the creature has more HD than the brigand’s class level, it receives a +4 circumstance bonus on this save.

This ability is in addition to the effects of threatening appearance and blatant threat. Once a creature has been the target of this ability (regardless of whether or not the saving throw is successful), it is immune to that brigand’s stunning appearance for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect.

Quick Thinking (Ex)

At 20th level, a brigand can size up an enemy as a free action once per round, and he can size up a number of creatures equal to his Intelligence modifier at a time.

Favored Class Bonuses
Archfiends: Add a +1/2 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the bridand’s favored weapon (maximum bonus +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Ar’kesh: Gain 1/6 of a vigilante social talent.
Bladebearer: Add a +1/2 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the bridand’s favored weapon (maximum bonus +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Dathomin: Gain 1/6 of a rogue talent.
Demon-Blooded: Gain a +1/2 bonus on Stealth checks against the target of your subtle threat.
Drakorin: Add +1/2 to sneak attack damage dealt to creatures with the dragon type.
Glaedris: Add +1/2 to damage rolls the brigand makes with favored weapon attacks against an opponent he is flanking or an opponent that is denied its Dexterity bonus to AC.
Goblin: Add a +1/2 bonus on Stealth checks and Perception checks made in dim light or darkness.
God-Blooded: Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to feint and Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Human: Choose an environment from the ranger’s favored terrain list. Gain +1/3 on all Acrobatics, Climb, and Stealth checks in the chosen areas.
Orc: Add a +1/2 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the bridand’s favored weapon (maximum bonus +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Pixie: Add +1/2 to sneak attack damage dealt to creatures with the fey type.
Squidling: Gain a +1/2 bonus on Disguise checks.
Ticaru: Increase the DC of subtle threat by +1/3. This does not stack with other feats or abilities that increase DC.
Tiefling: Add +1/2 to sneak attack damage dealt to creatures with the outsider type.
Torn: Gain a +1/2 bonus on Stealth checks against the target of your subtle threat.
